posts.name: Gorbachev
posts.cooked:
Hard disagree on that, for the simple fact that there’s a lot of other things which, narratively, should be still able to be accomplished yet are locked for people who weren’t playing at the time, including the rewards.

Trivializing an accomplishment that most people of a class didn’t do because of its difficulty (or simply not knowing about it/not caring about it) serves no purpose. The title is a sign of distinction for factors that are no longer at play. If you could guarantee those factors, then I’d be amenable, but if you can trivialize content that was specifically designed to be difficult even at the time, the specific reward provided should be trivialized as well.

For example, I think Death’s Demise and The Immortal/The Undying are two of the coolest titles in the game, and even though I played OG Wrath, I didn’t get them. It sucks, but I just couldn’t accomplish what needed to be accomplished at the time. It happens. But if I wanted to do those things, I had WoW Classic available. I just don’t/didn’t care enough to go back even when given the opportunity to do so.

So, unless they can stringently timewalk the questline (which they aren’t going to do), or we make it to Classic Mists, don’t bring back the title unless they do it for all of the other rewards that are no longer available. Sometimes current content should remain current content.
